title: Using bribeR

First, start selecting conversations media manipulation counting speakers speak conversations:  Second, let’s say ’re interested making aggregate conclusions type speaker ’s speaking conversations. requires crossing corpus media transcripts speaker-level metadata.
code: library(ggplot2)  # Step 1: find transcript IDs about media  media_ids <- get_transcript_id(topic = "media")  # Step 2: load just those transcripts about the media  media_transcripts <- read_transcripts(id = media_ids)  # Step 3: count words spoken per speaker media_transcripts |>   mutate(n_words = lengths(strsplit(speech, "\\s+"))) |>   group_by(speaker_std) |>   summarise(total_words = sum(n_words, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>   arrange(desc(total_words)) |>   ## drop the 'background' and 'desconocido' to focus on identifiable speakers only   filter(speaker_std != "desconocido" & speaker_std != "background") |>   head(10) |>   ggplot(aes(x = reorder(speaker_std, total_words), y = total_words, fill = speaker_std)) +   geom_col() + coord_flip() + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +   theme(legend.position = "none") +   labs(     title = "Words spoken in media-related transcripts, \n top-10 most likely speakers",     x     = NULL,     y     = "Total words"   ) # Step 1: Left join media_transcripts with speaker-level metadata from `speakers` media_transcripts <- media_transcripts |>   left_join(speakers |> select(speaker_std, type, position),     by = "speaker_std"   )  ## Step 2: Count words spoken in media_transcripts and group by type, summarize media_transcripts |>   mutate(n_words = lengths(strsplit(speech, "\\s+"))) |>   group_by(type) |>   summarise(total_words = sum(n_words, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>   arrange(desc(total_words)) |>      filter(is.na(type) == F) |> #Filter only to identified speakers   ggplot(aes(x = reorder(type, total_words), y = total_words, fill = type)) +   geom_col() + coord_flip() + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +   theme(legend.position = "none") +   labs(     title = "Words spoken in media-related transcripts, by speaker type",     x     = NULL,     y     = "Total words"   )

text: bribeR R package accessing analyzing text transcript data Vladivideos, covert recordings documenting bribery corruption Alberto Fujimori’s presidency Peru (1990-2000). package provides user-friendly access large digital archive Vladivideo transcripts metadata, including data 139 individuals named files 15 expert-coded topics importance Fujimori presidency.  Speakers topics recorded Vladivideo files, Montesinos center. See Network Visualization details.

title: bribeR: Download, Process, and Analyze Vladivideos Transcripts
text: install package console, run one two commands:
code: # Install from CRAN install.packages("bribeR")  # Or install the development version from GitHub # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("jessietrudeau/bribeR")

title: bribeR: Download, Process, and Analyze Vladivideos Transcripts
text: package provides three families functions access, organize, analyze Vladivideo data. full online guide, see bribeR User Guide. 1. Read transcripts functions load transcript data tibbles load original source .csv files. 2. Find transcripts functions allow user filter transcripts specific speakers, topics, transcript ID numbers. 3. Integrate transcript metadata functions allow user integrate transcript-level metadata full-text transcripts information speakers.

title: bribeR: Download, Process, and Analyze Vladivideos Transcripts
text: syntax bribeR designed help users easily find download transcripts relevant interest. example, user interested obtaining transcript text data metadata conversations involving media manipulation run following lines code:
code: # Load data  library(bribeR)  # Find specific transcripts about media manipulation media_ids <- get_transcript_id(topic = "media")  # Get the metadata summary of the transcripts about media manipulation meta <- read_transcript_meta_data(media_ids)  # Load full-text transcripts about media manipulation media_transcripts <- read_transcripts(media_ids)

title: Read transcript-level metadata (id, date, speakers, duration, topics) — read_transcript_meta_data
text: Builds tidy data frame transcript metadata bundled package data. Combines information three internal sources: transcript_index (transcript identifiers, dates, topic flags), speakers_per_transcript (speaker roster per transcript), compiled_transcripts (word counts derived speech column).

title: Read transcript-level metadata (id, date, speakers, duration, topics) — read_transcript_meta_data
text: id Optional numeric vector transcript IDs return metadata (e.g., 5, c(5, 12, 47)). NULL (default), metadata every transcript returned. IDs matching transcript dropped warning naming . quiet Logical; FALSE, prints progress messages. Default TRUE.

title: Read transcript-level metadata (id, date, speakers, duration, topics) — read_transcript_meta_data
text: tibble one row per transcript columns: id (numeric): transcript identifier. date (Date): date associated transcript (NA absent). speakers (list character): unique, sorted vector speakers transcript. n_words (integer): total word count across transcript's speech column. topics (list character): vector topic names inferred topic_* flags.

title: Read transcript-level metadata (id, date, speakers, duration, topics) — read_transcript_meta_data
text: Transcript ID (id) date: Read bundled transcript_index dataset. Topics (topics list-column): Columns transcript_index whose names start topic_ interpreted topic flags (1/0 integers). Topic names normalized removing topic_ prefix replacing _ spaces. Speakers (speakers list-column): Read bundled speakers_per_transcript dataset. Speaker columns collapsed unique, sorted character vector per transcript. Duration (n_words): Computed bundled compiled_transcripts dataset summing whitespace-delimited tokens speech column unique transcript id.

title: bribeR 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Provides access 95 Vladivideos transcripts, holding 45,337 speech turns, via read_transcripts(), get_transcript_id(), get_transcript_speakers(), get_transcripts_raw(), read_transcript_meta_data(). five functions take transcript numbers id argument. Includes run_transcript_network_app(), interactive Shiny application visualizing Speaker-Topic Speaker Co-Appearance networks. Bundles five datasets: compiled_transcripts, transcript_index, speakers_per_transcript, speakers, topic_descriptions.
